text: RETRACTED (switch_clock): 'TXC-post beats the per-token SAE, so a window sees what one position cannot.' A raw probe on the single label position reaches r=0.31-0.37 there, above every dictionary. The dictionary gap was real but measures code efficiency, not temporal structure. Caught before publication by the raw gate.
On the trailing novelty rate, the paper's TXC (post-squash) at T=8 beats the per-token SAE at matched code budget
...and beats T-SAE, the temporal baseline the paper compares against
...and beats Stacked SAE at the SAME window size, which isolates the shared cross-position code from merely seeing a window (reviewer bbby's ablation)

BUDGET-QUALIFIED (audit F2 correctly failed the unqualified form): TXC-pre reaches +0.480 at T=8, above TXC-post's +0.463 — but on 35.2 active latents versus 17.2, roughly twice the code budget, so it is not a matched comparison. At a matched budget TXC-pre's best cell is T=4 at +0.359. The matched-budget winner is TXC-post at T=8. TXC-pre's budget cannot be calibrated down at large T because it keeps k actives per position and sums them (l0 reaches 145 at T=16 and 551 at T=32); those cells are excluded from every headline.
